target.title: fix(ui): Realtime Talk hangs when Google Live connections stall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI users starting Realtime Talk with Google Live could remain stuck in the connecting state when the browser WebSocket never opened or opened without Google ever completing protocol setup. During that stall, the microphone, camera stream, input meter, and both audio contexts could remain active indefinitely. A socket error or close before readiness could leave the same resources active until the user manually dismissed the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser WebSocket construction has no caller-configurable startup deadline, so the Google Live transport now owns a 30-second deadline covering the full startup phase through the current socket's Google `setupComplete` frame. This matches the existing Realtime Talk WebRTC setup deadline while using the provider-specific readiness signal documented by the [Google Live API](https://ai.google.dev/api/live), instead of treating the lower-level WebSocket `open` event as ready.

Timeout, error, and close paths report the transport error and stop the current socket lifecycle exactly once. Captured-socket checks before and after asynchronous message decoding keep stale socket events from clearing a replacement attempt's timer or emitting readiness for it. The conflict resolution with the merged Gemini Live video work preserves camera-frame shutdown, media-track release, and `onVideoStream(null)` cleanup.

## User Impact

Google Live Realtime Talk now fails with a clear error instead of connecting forever when either the WebSocket handshake or Google protocol setup stalls. Failed, closed, and timed-out attempts release the microphone, camera, input meter, socket, and both AudioContext instances without waiting for another user action.

## Evidence

Frozen and independently reviewed product patch:

- Base: `047232bd16e407cf53762eb6ffa80d400b1d249e`
- Exact head: `50b8114a49af3409d82994041bf5f43dcb2b5db9`
- Diff SHA-256: `310e8f132bb1b8c4d38f12423e7d8dc42532d3ace56003972bbef2ddd599c1d2`
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review found no actionable issue after checking the full transport, callers, sibling realtime transports, current camera lifecycle, and focused tests.

### Immutable Chromium before/after proof

[Fork workflow run 29671173448](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29671173448) checked out the two immutable product revisions above, started the production Control UI, and drove the real **Start voice input** control in Playwright Chromium. It used Chromium fake microphone/camera devices and a controlled Google WebSocket that opened but withheld `setupComplete`; no provider secret was used or captured.

- Baseline at `047232bd`: after 30,000 ms the UI still showed Connecting; the microphone track remained live, both AudioContexts remained open, all five audio nodes remained connected, the meter interval remained active, and the WebSocket remained open.
- Candidate at `50b8114`: after the same 30,000 ms the UI visibly showed `Realtime connection timed out after 30000ms`; the real Chromium fake-microphone track changed from live to ended, both AudioContexts closed, all five audio nodes disconnected, the processor callback was removed, the 100 ms meter interval cleared, and the WebSocket closed.
- Healthy control on both revisions: the provider returned `setupComplete`, the UI entered Listening, enabled the Chromium fake camera, and remained healthy beyond 30 seconds. Manual Stop then ended both the audio and video tracks, closed both AudioContexts and the WebSocket, disconnected all audio nodes, and cleared the meter interval.

Artifacts include full-page before/after screenshots and machine-readable resource snapshots:

- [Baseline artifact](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29671173448/artifacts/8437355889)
- [Candidate artifact](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29671173448/artifacts/8437347376)

The UI intentionally disables camera activation while status is Connecting, so the stalled browser path owns only the microphone. The healthy browser control proves the real camera lifecycle; the focused video regression directly enables camera before readiness and proves timeout cleanup of its track and `onVideoStream(null)` callback.

### Tests and CI

- Exact-head [CI run 29670170917](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29670170917): `checks-ui`, build, production/test types, lint, QA profiles, security, workflow sanity, and every other Node shard passed. The focused Google Live suites passed 30 tests, including pre-open timeout, open-without-`setupComplete`, successful setup deadline clearing, error/close idempotence, manual stop, stale socket ownership, and camera cleanup.
- The only red job was unrelated `src/cli/acp-cli-exit.process.test.ts` in `checks-node-compact-small-7`; this PR changes only three `ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-google-live*` files. The same five ACP tests [passed on the frozen base SHA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29669273040/job/88145536269), while the PR run's other 3,127 shard tests passed.
- A bounded live observation against Google's real constrained WebSocket endpoint with an intentionally invalid probe token established the relevant post-open/no-application-readiness state: `{"reason":"watchdog","elapsedMs":15060,"readyState":2,"events":[{"type":"open","ms":812}]}`.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.
